title: All the Fish in the Stream

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — JUSTICE AND CONSEQUENCES (JUS-01 to JUS-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Everyday rules, disputes between neighbors, the elders and the council, making things right, losing a role, a night to cool down, wrongful suspicion and evidence that doesn't add up. Consequences are proportionate and never cruel; children get guidance; nobody goes without food, water or shelter; an accusation is not guilt.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A villager's fish traps block the whole stream, and a fisher downstream catches nothing: ask the elders, or talk at the stream.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has set fish traps all the way across the stream, bank to bank, and (subject.his/her) catches have never been better. (friend), who fishes further downstream, hasn't caught a single fish in a week. Today (friend) has walked upstream and found out why.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "You've closed off the whole stream," says (friend). (subject) looks at the traps as if seeing them for the first time. "...I never thought about downstream." (subject.He/she) opens a wide gap in the middle. A few days later, (friend) brings (subject.him/her) the first fish (friend.he/she) catches, out of a sort of fairness.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: The elders rule that a stream belongs to everyone who fishes it: traps may reach halfway across, never the whole way. (subject) moves half of them, a bit grudgingly. Within days (friend) is catching fish again, and (subject) is catching nearly as many as before, which surprises them both.
